newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- JUNE 20.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--A US Pentagon map issued at the end of last year shows the Aegean islet of Imia as clearly belonging to Greece, US defence department spokesman Kenneth Bacon said yesterday. Previous maps had shown Imia to be of "unknown sovereignty" but the change came about, Bacon said, after directions from the State Department. The State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said he was unaware of any such directives.

--Labour and Social Security Minister Miltiades Papaioannou yesterday received assurances from the finance and economy ministries that 27.17 billion drachmas owed to the Social Security Foundation in contributions would be recovered from debtors.

--A new tourism bill presented yesterday provides for 10,000 businesses such as restaurants to receive national and EU subsidies to upgrade hygiene on their premises. The cost is estimated at 3.5 billion drachmas.
--The problem of employment can only be resolved through "liberal" policies, National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou is reported to have said yesterday.
--Various social groups have called for an investigation into television "reality shows" following the suicide of a 47-year-old man unwillingly subjected to the camera's glare.
--The Spraou report commissioned by the government on how the economy can achieve convergence has recommended contained wage increases for the next two years.
--Insurance companies are considering increasing premiums for hospitalisation and slowly reforming policies on health care due to overwhelming costs.

--The interior ministry has announced new criteria for the selection of would-be civil servants. Changes to the public sector include evaluation of the performance of civil servants and employees' evaluation of managers.
--The Wild One Marlon Brando is in Greece at the invitation of the Latsis shipping family to speak on environmental issues. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
